_comment: Auth provisioning input for Deploy-WwExecutionEngine.ps1 (-AuthConfigPath).
Maps directly onto Configure-WwExecutionAuth.ps1 -GroupPermissions / -UserAssignments.
GroupPermissions: each key is an Entra app role / group name; the value is
an array of Permission.* roles auto-assigned alongside the group role to
every user mapped to that group (empty array = group role only).
Every key becomes an app role on the resource app with allowedMemberTypes
['User','Application'], so it is assignable both to users and to app-only
clients (daemon / Managed Identity service principals).
UserAssignments: each entry maps a user UPN to one of the groups above.
A UPN whose Group has no GroupPermissions entry receives only the group role.
Client apps (app-only callers such as the AzureFunction / ServiceBus examples
calling the engine with a Managed Identity or client-credentials token)
CANNOT be listed in UserAssignments - that section is UPN-only. Instead:
1. Keep a group for them in GroupPermissions (e.g. Warewolf_ClientApps)
so the app role exists on the resource app.
2. Assign that role to the client's service principal / Managed Identity
via Configure-WwExecutionAuth-Clients.ps1 (or the per-example
Configure-WwExecutionAuth-ClientApps.ps1) with
-AppRolesToAssign Warewolf_ClientApps - a roleless app-only caller
carries no 'roles' claim and is rejected by the engine.
3. Add a matching secure.config WindowsGroupPermissions row
(WindowsGroup = the app-role value, per-workflow IsServer=false,
Execute=true) - the token's roles claim only authorizes what
secure.config grants.
Note: Entra sanitizes app-role values (runs of disallowed characters
become '_'), so the secure.config WindowsGroup must use the sanitized
value, e.g. 'Warewolf ClientApps' -> 'Warewolf_ClientApps'.
Copy this file (drop the _comment), edit the values, and pass it via
-AuthConfigPath ./Deploy-WwExecutionEngine.authconfig.json
